name: What is OpenStack?
description:
OpenStack is a free and open-source cloud computing software platform.Users primarily deploy it as an Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) solution.
OpenStack software controls large pools of compute, storage, and networking resources throughout a datacenter, managed through a Dashboard or API.
Do you know who started OpenStack?
answer: In July 2010, Rackspace Hosting and NASA jointly launched an open-source cloud-software initiative known as OpenStack. Now More than 200 companies have joined this project.

name: OpenStack components and DevStack
description:
OpenStack has a modular architecture with various code names for its components. Here are the list of basic components. 
OpenStack Identity (keystone)

OpenStack dashboard (horizon)

OpenStack Compute (nova) 

OpenStack Object Storage (swift) 

OpenStack Block Storage (cinder)

OpenStack Image service (glance)

OpenStack Networking (neutron, formerly quantum)
Lets have some background about these important components

Compute (Nova)

OpenStack Compute (Nova) is a cloud computing fabric controller, which is the main part of an IaaS system.It is designed to manage and automate pools of computer resources and can work with widely available virtualization technologies like KVM, VMware, and Xen together with Hyper-V and Linux container technology such as LXC

Image Service (Glance)

OpenStack Image Service (Glance) provides discovery, registration, and delivery services for disk and server images. Stored images can be used as a template.

Dashboard (Horizon)

OpenStack Dashboard (Horizon) provides administrators and users a graphical interface to access, provision, and automate cloud-based resources.

Identity Service (Keystone)

OpenStack Identity (Keystone) provides a central directory of users mapped to the OpenStack services they can access. It acts as a common authentication system across the cloud operating system and can integrate with existing backend directory services like LDAP. It supports multiple forms of authentication including standard username and password credentials, token-based systems and AWS-style (i.e. Amazon Web Services) logins.

Networking (Neutron)

OpenStack Networking (Neutron, formerly Quantum) is a system for managing networks and IP addresses. OpenStack Networking ensures the network is not a bottleneck or limiting factor in a cloud deployment, and gives users self-service ability, even over network configurations.

Block Storage (Cinder)

OpenStack Block Storage (Cinder) provides persistent block-level storage devices for use with OpenStack compute instances. The block storage system manages the creation, attaching and detaching of the block devices to servers.

name: Install and Configure DevStack
description:
Devstack is used for development and is probably the fastest and easiest way to deploy OpenStack.
Lets begin with installation of DevStack . Remember you can either type below commands manually or simply copy/paste them using browser into right side terminal. We will update our system and install git, we need git to clone openstack repos
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get -y install git

Now lets add sudo user, we need to install DevStack as non-root. We are creating new user in a non-interactive mode (thus avoiding stuffs like phone,real-name etc) and it has no password.
sudo adduser --disabled-password --gecos "" stack
sudo su
echo "stack ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" >> /etc/sudoers

Lets switch to the new account
sudo su stack
cd /home/stack
Right time to fetch the DevStack repo
git clone https://git.openstack.org/openstack-dev/devstack -b kilo-2 openstack

Lets create a local.conf file with basic password and stable repo details then enable swift and networking services.
cd /home/stack/openstack 
echo '[[local|localrc]]' > local.conf
echo ADMIN_PASSWORD=password >> local.conf
echo MYSQL_PASSWORD=password >> local.conf
echo RABBIT_PASSWORD=password >> local.conf
echo SERVICE_PASSWORD=password >> local.conf
echo SERVICE_TOKEN=tokentoken >> local.conf
echo CINDER_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo GLANCE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo HORIZON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo KEYSTONE_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo NEUTRON_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo NOVA_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf
echo SWIFT_BRANCH=stable/kilo >> local.conf

Just one more thing to add before running the script. We need to set HOST_IP. You can fetch it from /root/ directory. Just do
sudo ls /root
52.11.130.199 tmp
the ip-address will be different for you, so update properly and execute the script as user 'stack'. 
echo HOST_IP=52.11.130.199 >> /home/stack/openstack/local.conf
./stack.sh
This installation will take around 20 to 30 minutes, please feel free leave this machine and take a break :)

Do you know what tasks the script script.sh will perform?
answer:
1. Downloads OpenStack code from git repo.
2. Install OpenStack components and resolves any dependencies
3. Start OpenStack components/services.

name: Log into Dashboard
description:
Congrats! Now you have basic OpenStack setup ready for use! That's pretty easy, right?

Now you need to access OpenStack Dashboard, horizon. So point your browser to your HOST_IP ipaddress 
 http://HOST_IP
You will see the OpenStack Dashboard Login page, use admin/password to complete login process.

What's OpenStack Horizon?
answer: Horizon is the canonical implementation of OpenStack's Dashboard, which provides a web based user interface to OpenStack services.

name: Create an Instance
description:
Once logged in you can see System tab on Dashboard. Click on System-> System Information to view services and its status. Now click on Compute tab on Dashboard left side. Follow these menu :
Compute-> Instances -> Launch Instance
Now provide Instance name as webminal_openstack.Set Instance boot Source as "Boot from Image" and select cirros from the next box


cirros is a minimal Linux distribution. Submit Launch . Wait for few seconds, the instance will be up and running. Can you see the ipaddress of this instance? Just login into this instance using username cirros with password cubswin:)

ssh cirros@instance-ip

Cool :) You Installed,Configured and Launched an instance under OpenStack cloud environment! We will explore about OpenStack more in upcoming sessions! Until then feel free to play around with OpenStack setup. Please share us any feedback or comments. Happy Learning!
